'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Middle Eastern crisis (2023–present)|Middle Eastern crisis]]
**[[Israeli–Palestinian conflict]]
***[[Gaza war]]
****[[2025 Gaza City offensive]]
*****Four [[Israeli Ground Forces|Israeli soldiers]] are [[killed in action|killed]] by [[Hamas]] on the outskirts of [[Gaza City]] in the [[Gaza Strip]]. [https://www.timesofisrael.com/liveblog_entry/idf-announces-four-soldiers-killed-in-hamas-attack-on-army-camp-outside-gaza-city/ (''The Times of Israel'')]
***[[Palestinian political violence]]
****[[2025 Ramot Junction shooting]]
*****Six people are killed and seven others are wounded in a [[mass shooting]] targeting [[Israelis]] by [[Palestine|Palestinian]] assailants in [[Jerusalem]]. The two perpetrators are killed following a [[shootout]] with [[Israel Defense Forces|a soldier]] and a civilian. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/cr70ny0l7vgo (BBC News)] [https://edition.cnn.com/2025/09/08/middleeast/jerusalem-attack-dozen-injured-intl (CNN)]
**[[Israel–Hezbollah conflict (2023–present)|Israel–Hezbollah conflict]]
***Five people are killed and five others injured during at least eight Israeli [[airstrike]]s between [[Beqaa Valley]] and [[Hermel]], in [[Lebanon]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2025/9/8/israeli-strikes-kill-five-in-lebanon-in-latest-ceasefire-breach (Al Jazeera)]
*[[War in the Sahel]]
**[[Mali war]]
***[[Jama'at Nasr al-Islam wal Muslimin]] (JNIM) imposes a nationwide blockade on fuel and other goods imported from neighboring countries while besieging [[Malian government]]-held cities and towns. An unknown number of fuel trucks from [[Senegal]] and the [[Ivory Coast]] violating JNIM's blockade have been attacked and burned by militants. [https://apnews.com/article/mali-fuel-al-qaeda-blockade-jnim-sikasso-8ec3906c16721ee128718d9f2c21c1d4 (AP)]
***The [[Malian Armed Forces|Malian army]] conducts [[airstrike]]s in the [[Kayes Region]] against JNIM, reporting operations in [[Diéma, Mali|Diema]] and [[Nioro du Sahel]] that included freeing hostages. [https://www.reuters.com/world/africa/mali-army-carries-out-airstrikes-after-militants-announce-blockade-fuel-imports-2025-09-08/ (Reuters)]
*[[Kivu conflict]]
**[[Allied Democratic Forces insurgency]]
***According to a local leader, 102 people are killed when [[Allied Democratic Forces]] rebels attack a funeral in Ntoyo, [[North Kivu]], [[Democratic Republic of the Congo]]. [https://www.aa.com.tr/en/africa/at-least-70-killed-in-suspected-adf-rebels-attack-on-funeral-in-eastern-dr-congo/3682384 (Anadolu Agency)] [https://www.euronews.com/2025/09/09/is-group-linked-militants-slaughter-60-people-in-eastern-dr-congo (Euronews)]
*[[2025 Nepalese Gen Z protests]]
**[[Nepal Police|Police]] open fire on protesters demonstrating against a [[government of Nepal|government]] ban on [[social media]] in [[Kathmandu]], [[Nepal]], killing at least 19 people and wounding over a hundred more. A [[curfew]] is declared around all government buildings, including the [[Rastrapati Bhawan]] and [[Federal Parliament of Nepal|Federal Parliament]]. [https://www.cbc.ca/news/world/nepal-deadly-protests-1.7627595 (CBC News)] [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/c78nd2zy9jgo (BBC News)] [https://news.sky.com/story/at-least-14-dead-in-nepal-protests-over-social-media-ban-13427038 (Sky News)]
**[[Ramesh Lekhak]] resigns as [[Minister of Home Affairs (Nepal)|Minister of Home Affairs]] in response to the [[Police brutality|police killings]] of protesters. [https://www.firstpost.com/world/nepal-home-minister-resigns-takes-moral-responsibility-after-violent-gen-z-protests-leave-20-dead-13931943.html (Firstpost)]
**Nepal's [[Ministry of Information and Communications (Nepal)|Ministry of Information and Communications]] lifts [[Censorship in Nepal|its ban]] on major [[social media]] platforms following the protests. [https://www.france24.com/en/live-news/20250909-major-social-media-sites-back-online-in-nepal-after-deadly-protests (AFP via France 24)]

'''Business and economy'''
*[[Succession of Rupert Murdoch]]
**The [[Murdoch family#Fourth generation|children]] of [[News Corporation|News Corp]] founder and former chairperson [[Rupert Murdoch]] reach a [[Settlement (litigation)|settlement]] over the corporation's control, transferring all [[Share (finance)|shares]] held by the original [[family trust]] to a new entity which gives [[Lachlan Murdoch|Lachlan]] sole voting control, while [[Prudence MacLeod|Prudence]], [[Elisabeth Murdoch (businesswoman)|Elisabeth]], and [[James Murdoch|James]] exit with a reported US$3.3 billion settlement. [https://www.france24.com/en/business/20250909-murdoch-heirs-media-empire (AFP via France 24)]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*[[2025 Atlacomulco bus crash]]
**A train collides with a [[double-decker bus]] at a [[level crossing]] in [[Atlacomulco]], [[Mexico]], killing at least ten people and injuring 41 others. [https://ca.news.yahoo.com/train-collision-bus-mexico-kills-162243311.html (Yahoo! News Canada)]

'''International relations'''
*[[Israel–Spain relations]]
**Spain announces an indefinite ban on ships transporting fuel and planes carrying weaponry to Israel from all of its [[port]]s and [[airspace]] in response to the [[Gaza genocide]]. [https://www.politico.eu/article/spain-pm-sanchez-permanent-weapons-embargo-israel/ (''Politico'')]
**[[Spain]] recalls its [[ambassador]] to [[Israel]] after the [[Cabinet of Israel|Israeli government]] accused [[Prime Minister of Spain|Spanish prime minister]] [[Pedro Sánchez]] of being "[[Antisemitism|antisemitic]]" and barred two Spanish officials from entering Israel, with [[List of foreign ministers of Spain|Spanish foreign minister]] [[José Manuel Albares]] calling it "slanderous accusations" against the country. [https://www.barrons.com/news/spain-recalls-ambassador-to-israel-over-antisemitism-spat-812f1f88 (''Barron's'')]
*[[Belarus–Czech Republic relations]]
**The [[Czech Republic]] expels a [[Belarus]]ian diplomat accused of [[espionage]] after cooperating with [[Romanian Intelligence Service|Romania]]n and [[Információs Hivatal|Hungarian intelligence services]] to dismantle a [[State Security Committee of the Republic of Belarus|Belarusian spy network]] in Europe. [https://www.reuters.com/world/czech-republic-expel-belarusian-diplomat-over-alleged-espionage-2025-09-08/ (Reuters)]
*[[2025 Georgia Hyundai plant immigration raid]]
**The [[South Korea]]n [[Ministry of Foreign Affairs (South Korea)|foreign ministry]] charters a plane to [[Repatriation|repatriate]] more than 300 [[South Koreans]] who were detained during an [[Immigrations and Customs Enforcement|ICE]] raid at a [[Hyundai]] plant in [[Ellabell, Georgia|Ellabell]], [[Georgia (US state)|Georgia]], [[United States]], last Thursday. [https://www.npr.org/2025/09/06/nx-s1-5532604/hyundai-immigration-raid-georgia-south-korea (NPR)]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[Immigration policy of the second Trump administration]]
**[[Deportation in the second Trump administration]]
***The [[United States Department of Homeland Security]] launches "Operation Midway Blitz", an [[United States Immigration and Customs Enforcement|Immigration and Customs Enforcement]] crackdown on [[Illegal immigration to the United States|undocumented immigrants]] in [[Illinois]] with serious [[Criminal records in the United States|criminal records]], while [[Government of Illinois|state officials]] say they received no formal notice of the operation. [https://www.reuters.com/world/us/trump-administration-says-it-launches-ice-crackdown-illinois-2025-09-08/ (Reuters)]
*''[[E. Jean Carroll v. Donald J. Trump]]'', [[Donald Trump sexual misconduct allegations]], [[Personal and business legal affairs of Donald Trump]]
**The [[United States Court of Appeals for the Second Circuit]] rejects [[President of the United States|President]] [[Donald Trump]]'s bid on the grounds of [[presidential immunity]] to overturn the civil ruling of ''Carroll I'' (2019), upholding that Trump must pay $83,300,000 to [[sexual abuse]] victim [[E. Jean Carroll]] for [[defamation]]. [https://www.nytimes.com/2025/09/08/nyregion/trump-e-jean-carroll-defamation.html (''The New York Times'')] [https://www.reuters.com/legal/government/trump-fails-overturn-e-jean-carrolls-83-million-verdict-2025-09-08/ (Reuters)]
**The US [[House Oversight Committee]] releases a "[[Jeffrey Epstein's 50th birthday greeting album|birthday book]]" compiled for [[Jeffrey Epstein]] in 2003, which includes a note allegedly signed by President Donald Trump; the White House denies its authenticity. The book is part of a larger set of documents. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/cvgqnn4ngvdo (BBC)]
*[[Frédéric Péchier case]]
**[[French people|French]] doctor Frédéric Péchier is tried for allegedly intentionally poisoning 30 people, including twelve fatally, at two clinics in [[Besançon]], [[Bourgogne-Franche-Comté]], [[France]]. [https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/crl5ngj9zwgo (BBC News)]
*[[Phillips family disappearances]]
**Tom Phillips, a man who [[Kidnapping|kidnapped]] his three children during a dispute with their mother and brought them to a remote countryside in 2021, is fatally shot by a police officer [[Shootout|after shooting]] and critically injuring another officer in the head following a robbery at an [[agricultural supplies]] store in [[Waikato]], [[New Zealand]]. All the three children are rescued. [https://www.nzherald.co.nz/nz/marokopa-children-found-after-tom-phillips-killed-in-police-shooting/GAVRHEIFR5DSBPD3QVWCNSG72U/ (''The New Zealand Herald'')]
*[[2025 Balçova police station shooting]]
**Two police officers are killed and three other people are injured in a [[mass shooting]] at a police station in [[İzmir]], [[Turkey]]. The 16-year-old perpetrator is arrested. [https://wtop.com/world/2025/09/teenager-kills-2-officers-in-attack-on-turkish-police-station/ (WTOP)]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[2025 Ivorian presidential election]]
**[[Ivory Coast]]'s [[Constitutional Council (Ivory Coast)|Constitutional Council]] bars former [[President of the Ivory Coast|president]] [[Laurent Gbagbo]] and former [[Credit Suisse]] CEO [[Tidjane Thiam]] from running in the upcoming presidential election, while approving five candidacies including President [[Alassane Ouattara]] and Gbagbo's wife [[Simone Gbagbo|Simone]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/africa/ivory-coast-formally-bars-ex-credit-suisse-chief-presidential-race-2025-09-08/ (Reuters)]
*[[2025 Norwegian parliamentary election]]
**[[Norwegians]] vote to elect all 169 members of the [[Storting]] using [[Party-list proportional representation|party-list]] [[proportional representation]] in 19 [[Voting systems#Multiple-winner methods|multi-member]] constituencies. [https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/norwegians-vote-labour-party-narrowly-favoured-win-re-election-2025-09-08/ (Reuters)]
**The left-wing [[Red–green coalition (Norway)|red–green coalition]], led by the [[Labour Party (Norway)|Labour Party]], wins a majority with 87 seats, while the right-wing populist [[Progress Party (Norway)|Progress Party]] becomes the second biggest party with 48 seats and the centre-right [[Conservative Party (Norway)|Conservative Party]] has its worst performance in 20 years, with 24 seats. [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2025/sep/08/norways-labour-party-holds-narrow-lead-in-early-election-results (''The Guardian'')]
*[[2025 Norwegian Sámi parliamentary election]]
**The [[:simple:Sámi people of Norway|Norwegian]] [[Sámi people]] vote to elect all 39 members of the [[Sámi Parliament of Norway|Sámi Parliament]] of [[Norway]] using [[Party-list proportional representation|party-list]] [[proportional representation]] in seven [[Voting systems#Multiple-winner methods|multi-member]] constituencies. [https://www.nrk.no/sapmi/ohpihii-adjana-vahku-ovdalgo-samedikki-valgabohtosat-leat-aibbas-_ielgan-1.17559597 (NRK)]
*[[2024–2025 French political crisis]]
**The [[France|French]] [[Bayrou government]] collapses after losing a [[Motion of no confidence|vote of confidence]] in the [[National Assembly (France)|National Assembly]] by 364 votes to 194. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/live/c5yqgnzw759t (BBC News)]
*The [[Philippines|Philippine]] [[Senate of the Philippines|Senate]] elects [[Tito Sotto]] as [[President of the Senate of the Philippines|Senate president]], replacing [[Chiz Escudero]] after 15 senators voted for a leadership change that also realigned [[Senate of the Philippines#Majority bloc|majority]] and [[Senate of the Philippines#Minority bloc|minority blocs]]. [https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2025-09-08/philippine-senate-elects-new-head-as-corruption-scandal-builds (Bloomberg News)] [https://newsinfo.inquirer.net/2106201/escudero-ousted-sotto-is-new-senate-president (''Philippine Daily Inquirer'')]
*[[Indonesia]]n [[President of Indonesia|president]] [[Prabowo Subianto]] reshuffles [[Red and White Cabinet|his cabinet]], appointing four new ministers and one deputy minister and establishing a new department, the [[Ministry of Hajj and Umrah (Indonesia)|Ministry of Hajj and Umrah]]. The removal of [[List of ministers of finance (Indonesia)|finance minister]] [[Sri Mulyani]] causes a sharp drop in the country's [[IDX Composite|main stock market index]] as well as the [[Indonesian rupiah|rupiah]]. [https://en.tempo.co/read/2047100/prabowo-inaugurates-four-new-ministers-one-deputy-minister-in-cabinet-reshuffle (''Tempo'')] [https://www.reuters.com/world/asia-pacific/indonesia-replaces-respected-finance-minister-with-economist-promising-rapid-2025-09-08/ (Reuters)]
*[[Uganda]]n [[Uganda Police Force|police]] detain the deputy spokesperson of the [[Opposition (politics)|opposition party]] [[National Unity Platform]] (NUP) outside a [[Judiciary of Uganda|court]] in [[Kampala]] where he was attending a [[bail]] hearing for party members held on charges the NUP describes as politically motivated. [https://www.reuters.com/world/africa/police-detain-senior-ugandan-opposition-official-2025-09-08/ (Reuters)]
